Transfer
Adam Cuerden — restoration; source digitisation engineer unestablished Documented

Commons explicitly requires credit to both Adam Cuerden and commons.wikimedia.org for use of this restoration. The upstream original MP3 is about 3:21 while the restored stream is about 3:16; the processing that accounts for this difference is not reconstructed.

[1]

Unknown Unknown

No transfer date established. The Commons, Archive and YouTube upload dates are not treated as digitisation or restoration dates.

[1]
Processing
Restored by Adam Cuerden; detailed restoration settings unestablished Documented

Only the described processing is documented; no equipment, filter settings, pitch correction or speed correction is inferred.

[1]
Composition rights
Underlying Puccini composition and historical libretto are public domain where ordinary life-plus-70 terms apply; no modern edition is claimed cleared. Documented

Commons marks the historical work public domain. This does not by itself establish the sound recording’s rights; the recording basis is separately documented below.

[1] [9]
Recording rights
Rules 1 and 2 — attribution-only release of Adam Cuerden’s restoration; underlying sound recording commercially issued in 1907 and public domain in the United States. Documented

The restoration is not treated as unrestricted public domain. Commons’ explicit permission allows all uses with credit to Adam Cuerden and commons.wikimedia.org; the credit is included in the listening introduction and this dossier. DAHR’s issue MARC gives [1907]. The opened upstream Archive metadata supplies no licence URL and no non-commercial restriction. No worldwide public-domain claim for the restoration.

[1] [3] [4] [10]

Giacomo Puccini, La bohème: O soave fanciulla. Nellie Melba and Enrico Caruso, New York, 24 March 1907; Victor C-4326-1 / 95200. Restoration by Adam Cuerden, via commons.wikimedia.org. All uses of this restored file must credit Adam Cuerden and commons.wikimedia.org. Rights statement

  6. Illica and Giacosa — La bohème, Quadro primo — Closing duet: declarations, brief negotiation about going out, lovers leave together and final singing is marked outside. Used for passage-general dramatic structure, not source-recording spatialisation or word timings.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Royal Opera House — La bohème, 3 October 2017 cinema programme — Page 2, Acts I and IV: first meeting, café departure, two men recalling absent lovers, friends’ meal and Mimì’s later return.. Accessed 2026-10-17.

Julian Morton Moses — American Celebrity Recordings 1900–⁠1925, UCSB Historical Discographies edition — Introduction explains that artist sections group records by release years, not session dates. Caruso: Victor Red Seal 1906–⁠1908 includes 89006 and 95200; 1909–⁠1911 includes 87043. Destinn: Victor Red Seal 1914–⁠1917 includes 88487. Opened as extracted text; not used to infer exact take or transfer pressing.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
